Scalar parameter object for LMTP estimation

LMTPParameter.Rd

LMTPParameter is an R6 class representing a scalar target parameter in a longitudinal modified treatment policy problem.

The class is intentionally narrow. It does not fit nuisance functions or perform targeting itself. Instead, it defines:

  • the parameter name,

  • the scale of the target parameter,

  • how to compute the plug-in estimate from fitted regressions,

  • how to compute the efficient influence function contribution once nuisance functions are available.

The default implementation corresponds to the LMTP mean parameter \(\psi = \mathbb{E}[Y^d]\).

Public fields

name

Character name of the parameter.

outcome_type

Character outcome type, typically "continuous" or "binary".

scale

Character scale on which the parameter lives. Usually "identity".

Method plugin()

Compute the plug-in estimate from the final-stage regression.

Usage

LMTPParameter$plugin(ds, policy_seq, Q_list)

Arguments

ds

An LMTPData object.

policy_seq

An LMTPPolicySequence.

Q_list

List of fitted outcome regression functions. Each Q_list[[t]] should be a function (A_vec, H_df) -> numeric.

Details

For the LMTP mean parameter, the plug-in estimate is the empirical mean of the stage-1 shifted regression: $$ \psi_n = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \bar Q_1^d(H_{1,i}). $$

This method assumes Q_star_list[[1]] is a function of (A, H) returning the shifted regression at time 1 evaluated at A = d_1(A_1, H_1).

Returns

Numeric scalar estimate.

Method eif()

Compute the un-targeted EIF contribution.

Usage

LMTPParameter$eif(ds, policy_seq, Q_list, k_provider, psi = NULL)

Arguments

ds

An LMTPData object.

policy_seq

An LMTPPolicySequence.

Q_list

List of fitted outcome regression functions.

k_provider

Output of LMTPNuisanceFactory$k_provider(ds).

psi

Optional scalar plug-in estimate. If NULL, it is computed internally via $plugin().

Details

For the LMTP mean parameter, the EIF has the recursive form $$ D(O) = \sum_{t=1}^{\tau} \omega_t \left\{\bar Q_{t+1}^d - \bar Q_t^d\right\} + \bar Q_1^d - \psi, $$ where by convention \(\bar Q_{\tau+1}^d = Y\).

This method expects:

  • Q_list[[t]] gives \(\bar Q_t^d(A_t, H_t)\) via a function of (A, H),

  • k_provider$K_obs(t) returns \(\omega_t\),

  • policy_seq$apply_t(t, ...) computes the shifted treatment at time t.

Returns

Numeric vector of length n.

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 200

df <- data.frame(
  W1 = rnorm(n),
  L1 = rnorm(n)
)
df$A1 <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(0.5 * df$W1 - 0.7 * df$L1))
df$L2 <- rnorm(n, mean = 0.3 * df$A1 + 0.2 * df$W1)
df$A2 <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(-0.3 * df$W1 + 0.6 * df$L2))
df$Y  <- rnorm(n, mean = 0.5 * df$A1 + 0.7 * df$A2 + 0.3 * df$L2)

ds <- LMTPData$new(
  data = df,
  A_cols = c("A1", "A2"),
  L_cols = list("L1", "L2"),
  W_cols = "W1",
  Y_col = "Y"
)

pol <- mtp_discrete(
  map_fun = function(A, H) 1 - A,
  support = c(0, 1)
)
policy_seq <- repeat_policy_over_time(pol, tau = ds$tau())

nf <- LMTPNuisanceFactory$new(
  learners_g = nadir::lnr_logistic,
  policy_seq = policy_seq,
  A_type = "discrete",
  g_mode = "density"
)
#> Error in initialize(...): unused arguments (learners_g = function (data, formula, weights = NULL, ...) 
#> {
#>     learned_predictor <- lnr_glm(data = data, formula = formula, weights = weights, family = binomial(link = "logit"), ...)
#>     return(function(newdata) {
#>         learned_predictor(newdata)
#>     })
#> }, A_type = "discrete", g_mode = "density")
nf$train(ds)
#> Error: object 'nf' not found

q_fit_factory <- nf$q_trainer(
  learners_Q = nadir::lnr_glm
)
#> Error: object 'nf' not found

Q2 <- q_fit_factory(ds, t = 2, pseudo_outcome_vec = ds$Y())
#> Error in q_fit_factory(ds, t = 2, pseudo_outcome_vec = ds$Y()): could not find function "q_fit_factory"
Q1 <- q_fit_factory(ds, t = 1, pseudo_outcome_vec = Q2(ds$A(2), ds$H(2)))
#> Error in q_fit_factory(ds, t = 1, pseudo_outcome_vec = Q2(ds$A(2), ds$H(2))): could not find function "q_fit_factory"

param <- LMTPMean(outcome_type = "continuous")
psi <- param$plugin(ds, policy_seq, Q_list = list(Q1, Q2))
#> Error: object 'Q1' not found
psi
#> Error: object 'psi' not found

kp <- nf$k_provider(ds)
#> Error: object 'nf' not found
head(param$eif(ds, policy_seq, Q_list = list(Q1, Q2), k_provider = kp))
#> Error: object 'Q1' not found
